end_card.kicker: Starting with the cell. Working with the rhythms of life.

segments.headline: Why Timing Matters
segments.en: When we think about healthy ageing, it is not just a question of what we take. We also need to ask: when?

segments.headline: Daily Supplement
segments.en: Imagine you start paying more attention to nutrition. You choose a supplement, and remember to take it every day.

segments.headline: Delayed Lunch
segments.en: But when life gets busy, mealtimes keep changing. Lunch gets pushed back again.

segments.headline: Late Night Phone
segments.en: At night, a little more time on your phone turns into another late bedtime.

segments.headline: Inside the Cell
segments.en: So, is taking a supplement enough? To explore that question, let us look inside the cell: a city that works around the clock.

segments.headline: Mitochondria Energy
segments.en: Mitochondria are like power stations. They help supply the energy cells need to function.

segments.headline: Daily Movement
segments.en: Every walk, every movement, depends on energy supplied by your cells.

segments.headline: Lysosome Recycling
segments.en: This city also has recycling centres. Lysosomes break down and recycle some damaged proteins and cellular components.

segments.headline: DNA Repair
segments.en: There is maintenance work, too. DNA repair, for example, helps cells maintain the integrity of their genetic material.

segments.headline: Cellular Ageing
segments.en: As we age, some energy-producing, clearing and maintenance functions may become less effective. Damage can gradually accumulate, potentially affecting cells, tissues and organs.

segments.headline: Morning Light
segments.en: But cellular activity also follows a timetable. Morning light is an important signal that helps set that timing.

segments.headline: Circadian Coordination
segments.en: Light influences the master clock in the brain, which helps coordinate clocks in different organs and cells. Metabolism and some maintenance processes are regulated by circadian rhythms. Ageing, cellular function and these rhythms can also influence one another.

segments.headline: Winding Down
segments.en: That is why sleep and daily rhythms deserve attention together. But repair does not happen only at night. Different processes follow different rhythms.

segments.headline: Meal Timing Metabolism
segments.en: Mealtimes can also influence some peripheral clocks and metabolic rhythms. What we eat, and when we eat, are two questions worth considering together.

segments.headline: Ingredient Research
segments.en: Studying an ingredient is a little like studying how to improve one power station. To look after the whole city, we also need to consider the bigger picture.

segments.headline: Whole Body Systems
segments.en: Nutrition and metabolism provide materials and energy. Hormones carry regulatory signals, while the immune system also helps shape the cellular environment. Cellular function and whole-body systems continually influence one another.

segments.headline: Research to Practice
segments.en: This is the ASCLEPIOS HEALTH approach: a whole-system perspective, respect for biological rhythms, and practical application. Start with the foundations of diet, movement and sleep. Then consider nutritional support according to individual needs and evidence. What to use, how to use it, and when to use it must be considered individually. Not every supplement belongs in a fixed morning, afternoon or evening slot.

segments.headline: Invitation to Explore
segments.en: With ASCLEPIOS HEALTH, we will explore cellular energy, recycling and repair, and how body functions and biological rhythms can inform choices you can make every day. This journey towards healthy ageing begins with understanding yourself.

segments.headline: ASCLEPIOS HEALTH
segments.en: ASCLEPIOS HEALTH. Starting with the cell. Working with the rhythms of life.
